text:
maria: alert: EU-south hotpool showing sustained request queuing -> 99th token latency jumped to 2.4s, error spikes in KV cache slowpath. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/eu-south/hotpool
infra-bot: automated alert triggered: kvcache_slowpath_errors > 50/min, autoscaler_cooldown_active=true
aj: looking at the logs now. saw increased serialize time on kv_shard_17. suspect recent runtime jenkins build 2026-03-15:runtime-optimizations pushed last night
simon: any obvious CPU/GPU saturation? metrics look like GPU utilization is fine, but batcher queue length is climbing and IO wait on nodes hosting kv shards is high
li: can we offload to a compatible model variant in another region? EU-west1 has capacity but we need to confirm latency budget. we should avoid global failover if possible
rachael: cost note: cross-region egress for steady traffic will add ~20% per-100M tokens. we can short-term route critical routes only
maria: oncall-bot runbook step 2 suggests "drain hotpool and increase hotpool replicas" but draining will spike cold starts. prefer ramping replicas + traffic shaping
oncall-bot: runbook: https://playbooks.redwood/kvcache-slowpath -> recommended actions: increase_hotpool_replicas, enable_local_fallback_cache, divert_low-priority_traffic
aj: quick mitigation: enable local prefix caching (experimental) and temporarily reduce batch_max_tokens to 128 to reduce serialization overhead
simon: agree on reducing batch size. patch to runtime config ready:

```
PATCH /runtime/config
{"batch_max_tokens":128, "kvcache_prefetch":false}
```
li: executing traffic shaping to direct 30% of requests from eu-south -> eu-west1 for non-SLA customers
li: command:
```
redwood route update --from eu-south --to eu-west1 --selector "tier!=s1" --weight 30
```
maria: applied. watching metrics. queue length dropped ~18% in 60s but 99th still elevated
aj: started rolling back last runtime commit on 3 nodes hosting kv_shard_17. rollback id: runtime-2026-03-15-r1
aj: rollback in progress on node ids: i-0a12, i-0b34, i-0c56
simon: we should also temporarily increase hotpool SG to allow more concurrent kvcache workers. applying emergency config
simon: emergency config snippet:
```
hotpool.replicas += 4
kvcache.worker_threads = 48
```
rachael: reminder: increasing workers spikes GPU memory usage; watch oom signals
maria: logs show kvcache slowpath errors reduced after rollback on two nodes, full effect pending
li: traffic now 55% local, 30% eu-west, 15% overflow to na1 for retries. latency trend: 99th down from 2.4s -> 1.3s after 5m
oncall-bot: incident milestone: mitigated -> partial (service degraded). keep monitoring for 60m before closing
aj: follow-up: create postmortem link and include instrumented traces for batch serialization times. tentative owner: aj
rachael: can we estimate cost impact? li, can you run quick calc on extra replicas + cross-region egress for the 2h mitigation window
li: rough: +$6k for replicas + $4k cross-region egress for the window. will refine
maria: next steps: 1) run full revert of runtime patch during low-traffic window 2) add kvcache slowpath alert to page at 30/min (current was 50/min) 3) schedule perf regression triage with runtime team
simon: tagging runtime: @runtime-team for postmortem and kernel selection review
maria: thanks all. keeping thread open for updates. :pray:
